Conclusions & Recommendations . .-

In an attempt to satisfy the ALLS engine requirements, an advanced liquid rocket chamber cooling preliminary design based on current available information has been established. engines, a liner material of high thermal conductivity such as copper or a copper alloy is required. The typical fabrication method of a high chamber pressure liner is

to fabricate a forged billet from which coolant channels are milled and closed out with an electroformed material. The forging process itself is a long lead, high cost item. An alternative billet fabrication method is being investigated by Aerojet Propulsion Division which utilizes powder metal (P/M) and hot isostatic pressing (HIP) technologies. This method exhibits potential for both low cost and short fabrication time. Work is in progress to assess the feasibility of (P/M- HIP) forming of a zirconium-copper billet. The goal of the development activity is to establish a highly repeatable process which results in full size billets with high material properties. The work to date has demonstrated the feasibility of the process, and process parameters which result in 100% dense material with grain sizes approximately five times smaller than wrought have been determined. Shapes demonstrated to date have been a 2 . 0 inch I.D. and 3 . 5 inch O.D. cylinder and a billet approximately 1/4th the size of a

full scale ALS liner. Issues being investigated are powder oxidation prevention, optimization of mandrel design, material property assessment, process repeatability, and NDE assessment. The development activity will culminate in the

fabrication of up to six full scale ALS billets.
